summary: The Broadway Album is Barbra Streisand's twenty-fourth studio album, released by Columbia Records on November 5, 1985. Mostly classic show tunes, it marked a major shift after she spent much of the 1970s and 1980s singing rock, pop, folk and disco-oriented songs for Columbia. Stephen Sondheim wrote additional lyrics for two songs at Streisand's request, and the album was both a critical and commercial success, reaching four times platinum certification by 1995.
one_line: Barbra Streisand's 1985 Broadway show-tunes album, her twenty-fourth studio release, marking a major shift in her career.
key_facts: The Broadway Album is the twenty-fourth studio album by Barbra Streisand.
The Broadway Album was released by Columbia Records on November 5, 1985.
The album consists mainly of classic show tunes.
The album marked a major shift in Barbra Streisand's career.
Streisand spent ten years appearing in musicals and singing standards on her albums in the 1960s.
From the album 'Stoney End' in 1971 to the album 'Emotion' in 1984, Streisand sang mostly rock, pop, folk, and disco-oriented songs for Columbia records.
Stephen Sondheim personally penned additional lyrics for the songs 'Putting It Together' and 'Send in the Clowns' at the singer's request.
The album was originally released on the Columbia label and subsequently re-released by Columbia and Sony Records.
The album was a critical and commercial success.
The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) first certified the album gold on January 13, 1986.
The album reached four times platinum on January 31, 1995.
